DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
## What the paper claims

The paper recommends awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months. It rests on four claims:
- **Cheapest on price.** ParcelLine saves £35,000–£76,000 a year once the 70/30 weight mix is applied.
- **Met the service threshold.** All three carriers cleared the 95% on-time threshold in the trial.
- **Fewer customer contacts.** ParcelLine's tracking app roughly halved "where is my order?" (WISMO) contacts.
- **Flexible term.** The 12-month contract leaves room to re-tender.

I checked each against Table 1 and the paper's own cost figures.

## Summary

The price arithmetic is correct, and the trial is well designed: random allocation of about 5,000 parcels per carrier is a fair basis for comparison. But the paper's conclusions contradict its own trial results.
1. **ParcelLine failed two of the four requirements.** On-time delivery was **93.1%**, below the 95% threshold. The damage rate was **0.9%**, above the 0.5% limit.
2. **ParcelLine is the most expensive option overall.** The paper says damage and loss cost £48 per parcel. Including that, ParcelLine costs about **£8,100 a month more than SwiftDrop**.
3. **The tracking app's effect wasn't isolated.** For the second half of the trial, ParcelLine parcels also carried the new proactive text message.

On the paper's own figures, SwiftDrop is the stronger choice.

## 1. Arithmetic that checks out

- **Average cost per parcel at the 70/30 mix:** £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian.
- **Monthly cost at 42,000 parcels:** £149,100, £146,160 and £152,460.
- **Monthly price savings for ParcelLine:** £2,940 against SwiftDrop and £6,300 against Meridian, or £35,280 and £75,600 a year.
- **WISMO saving:** 210 fewer contacts × £3.20 = £672 a month against SwiftDrop.

As a price-list comparison, the figures are correct.

## 2. ParcelLine did not meet the requirements

| Requirement | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| On-time ≥ 95% | 96.2% ✓ | **93.1% ✗** | 97.5% ✓ |
| Damage < 0.5% | 0.4% ✓ | **0.9% ✗** | 0.3% ✓ |

Section 3's statement that on-time delivery "was above 95% for all three carriers," the recommendation's "met our service requirements," and the author's "all three carriers cleared our 95% threshold" all contradict Table 1.

**These gaps are not sampling noise.** With about 5,000 parcels per carrier:
- ParcelLine's on-time rate is several standard errors below 95%.
- Its damage rate, about 45 damaged parcels against about 20 for SwiftDrop, differs at roughly p ≈ 0.002.

**The lost-parcel figures carry little weight.** At this sample size they rest on single-digit counts of parcels.

## 3. Total cost including damage and loss

The paper says each damaged or lost parcel costs £48, but leaves this out of the cost comparison. Monthly figures at 42,000 parcels:

| | SwiftDrop | ParcelLine | Meridian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivery charges | £149,100 | £146,160 | £152,460 |
| Damaged and lost parcels | 181 | 412 | 134 |
| Damage and loss cost (× £48) | £8,670 | £19,760 | £6,450 |
| WISMO contacts (× £3.20) | £1,480 | £810 | £1,340 |
| **Total** | **£159,250** | **£166,730** | **£160,250** |

Even giving ParcelLine the full credit for its lower WISMO contacts, it costs about **£7,500 a month (£90,000 a year) more than SwiftDrop**. It also costs about £6,500 a month more than Meridian. The claimed saving of "up to £76,000 a year" reverses once the damage cost the paper itself cites is included.

These figures leave out the cost of late deliveries and of one-star reviews. Including them would widen ParcelLine's gap further.

## 4. The WISMO result is confounded

From 1 May, halfway through the trial, only ParcelLine parcels carried the new proactive delivery-day text. So ParcelLine's lower contact rate could come from:
- its tracking app;
- the text message;
- or both.

The statement that the app "clearly reduces customer contacts" is unsupported. The pattern is also unexpected: ParcelLine had the *worst* on-time rate, which would normally *raise* WISMO contacts. That makes the text message a plausible explanation.

**This can be settled with existing data.** Compare ParcelLine's WISMO rate in April, before the text, with May. If the text drove the reduction, rolling it out to whichever carrier you choose would capture the saving anyway.

## 5. Peak-season risk

The contract starts on 1 October, just ahead of peak season. ParcelLine's references are mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels. Your 30% heavier band is lamps, mirrors and small furniture, which are fragile and awkward to handle. ParcelLine's high damage rate fits that concern.

SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled peak volumes for retailers of similar size. The trial ran in April and May, outside peak, so all three carriers' on-time rates may be lower in November and December.

## 6. The comparison that remains

**SwiftDrop:**
- meets all requirements;
- is the cheapest on total cost;
- offers a 12-month term;
- has peak-season experience.

**Meridian:**
- has the best service, with 97.5% on-time and 0.3% damage;
- costs about £1,000 a month more than SwiftDrop on total cost;
- requires a 24-month term.

That difference is small relative to the uncertainty in the cost estimates. The real choice is whether Meridian's better reliability is worth a longer commitment.

**A split contract may be worth checking.** ParcelLine is cheapest for parcels under 2 kg (£2.85). If its damage and lateness came mainly from the heavier band, it could carry light parcels while SwiftDrop or Meridian carries heavy ones. That depends on trial results broken down by weight band, which the paper doesn't report. It also brings the complexity of managing two carriers.

## What is settled and what is open

**Settled by the paper's own figures:**
- ParcelLine failed the on-time and damage requirements.
- Including damage and loss, ParcelLine is the most expensive of the three.
- The WISMO reduction can't be attributed to the tracking app.

**Open, and what would settle each:**

| Question | What would settle it |
|---|---|
| Whether the app or the text cut WISMO contacts | ParcelLine's contact rate in April compared with May |
| Whether a split contract would work | On-time and damage rates by weight band for each carrier |
| Whether Meridian is worth the longer term | The value you place on its higher reliability, and the cost of a 24-month commitment |
| Peak-season performance | References from SwiftDrop's and Meridian's peak-season clients, and service-level terms covering peak |

## Recommendation

Don't award the contract to ParcelLine on this evidence. Revise the paper to:
1. report the trial results against the requirements accurately;
2. include damage, loss and contact costs in the cost comparison;
3. recommend SwiftDrop, or Meridian if the board values its reliability enough to accept 24 months;
4. note the split-contract option for follow-up if the weight-band data support it.

The trial was well designed. Its results point to a different carrier from the one the paper recommends.
